exploiter_exit_rate_per_hour.meaning: exit rate per hour achieved by a user splitting redemptions into frequent small transactions (redemptions every 5 minutes)
exploiter_exit_rate_per_hour.checkpoint: after repeated small redemptions over one hour

regular_exit_rate_per_hour.meaning: exit rate per hour achieved by a regular user making a single redemption
regular_exit_rate_per_hour.checkpoint: after a single redemption over one hour

speed_advantage_factor.meaning: reported speed advantage multiple of the exploiting user's exit rate over the regular user's exit rate

splitting_bypass_occurred.meaning: whether the redemption rate limit was bypassed by splitting redemptions across multiple transactions so that the same total blocked in one transaction became redeemable across several

assumptions: The report's rate-limit requirement is scoped to the same total redemption amount, so the comparison is made between exit rates over the same one-hour window.
Exit rates are reported as percentages of the user's position per hour; the comparison is at the amount/rate level as stated, not re-derived from a cap formula.
The exploiting user's scenario is redemptions every 5 minutes; the regular user's scenario is a single redemption.

unresolved.description: The report states the speed advantage as a 2.8x multiple and gives 71% vs ~30-40% exit rates, but supplies no numeric definition tying the exit rates to the 25%/30min cap formula, so the exact proportional relation between the cap and the observed rates cannot be derived; the plan compares the two reported exit rates directly.

No explicit precondition statements are supplied; the report does not establish a clean BEFORE state (prior market size, last-transaction timestamp, or caller authorization) separate from the exploit action, so precondition_ids is empty.

limitations: The selected impact is the speed advantage (2.8x faster exit); the 2.8x factor is recorded as a symbol but the relation predicate compares the reported exit rates rather than asserting the multiple as a formula.
The report's intent also covers a 25%/30min and 50%/hour cap; those numeric cap operands are not used as P because no precondition statement grounds them as a BEFORE fact.
The potential modality of the frequent-small-redemption action is preserved by treating the bypass as a scenario condition rather than an inevitable outcome.
